topic: OBS Studio ships 33.0.3, fixing the Windows startup crash that 33.0.2 caused on certain older CPUs
why_selected: The only story in the 24-hour pool whose central claims could be verified from an opened primary source under V7 rule 6b; it is practical for the creator's audience of streamers and recorders.
why_short: An OBS update crashed some older PCs; 33.0.3 fixes it.
why_beats_alternatives: Higher-scoring stories (OpenRouter prompt theft, Tesla FSD v15, Waymo recalls, UN autonomous-weapons talks, Amazon-Decart) could not be opened from this environment (openrouter.ai and npr.org failed with ENOTFOUND; x.com and news sites are blocked), so V7 rule 6b holds them. OBS 33.0.3 is modest news, but it is confirmed by the OBS Project's own release pages, opened directly, and it is something viewers can act on today.
why_this_story: OBS Studio 33.0.2 (20 Nov) could crash at startup on certain older processors; on 22 Nov the OBS team shipped 33.0.3 with the fix. It is practical: anyone who streams or records on an older Windows PC should update. X signal: none observed (x.com blocked; engagement UNKNOWN). It beat bigger stories only because they could not be verified by opening a source here.
verified_development: On 22 Nov 2026 the OBS Project published OBS Studio 33.0.3 on GitHub, marked Latest, with one hotfix: 'Fixed a crash on Windows in 33.0.2 with certain older CPUs'. 33.0.2 (20 Nov) had warned of a startup crash on certain older processors and told affected users to install 33.0.1 or 32.2.2.
disclosure: Disclosure: written by Claude, an Anthropic model. The OBS Project is not Anthropic; no conflict known.
research_summary: End-to-end test run (V7). The pool has 23 developments: 13 inside the 24-hour window (21-22 Nov) and 10 older context items, from fresh searches and leads from today's earlier research pass. Only anthropic.com and github.com opened; openrouter.ai and npr.org failed with ENOTFOUND and news, X, Reddit, YouTube and Instagram are blocked per the source audit. Every in-window story except OBS rests on search excerpts, so V7 rule 6b holds them. OBS Studio 33.0.3, released 22 Nov to fix a startup crash on certain older CPUs introduced in 33.0.2, is confirmed by its opened GitHub release pages and is today's eligible story.
key_facts: Known issue in 33.0.2: startup crash on certain older processors; 'does not affect everyone'.
33.0.3 released 22 Nov 2026, marked Latest: fixes the Windows crash in 33.0.2 with certain older CPUs.
OBS Studio is free and open source (GPL-2.0).
uncertainties: Which CPUs exactly are affected and how many users were hit is not stated.
Release times are shown without a year or time zone on the page; asset names and the page context place them in 2026.
No independent coverage was opened; the claims rest on the OBS Project's own release pages.
Whether 33.0.2's crash also affected macOS or Linux users is not stated; 33.0.3 names Windows.
excluded_claims: 'About 20 fixes' in 33.0.2 (a summariser's count, not checked line by line).
WebGPU for browser sources and other 33.0.2 items (not central).
context: OBS Studio is free, open-source streaming and recording software. 33.0.1 (29 Oct) and 33.0.2 (20 Nov) were hotfix releases on the 33.0 line.
script:
Did OBS crash on your Windows PC after updating this week? There's a fix.

On November 20, OBS Studio released version 33.0.2.

Then the team flagged a known issue. On certain older processors, OBS could crash at startup.

Their advice? Install an older version, like 33.0.1, until a fix arrived.

On November 22, it did. Version 33.0.3 fixes that Windows crash.

If you stream or record on an older PC, update now.

Did the crash hit you?
